newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Nov 26.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:
- More than 100,000 demonstrators protested in Belgrade against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
- U.S. broadcasting, consumer electronics and computer industries have agreed on a technical standard for the next generation of television.
- China has warned Walt Disney that the company's role in a film about the Dalai Lama might jeopardize its plans to invest in the country's entertainment industry.
- Two new government studies show that U.S. veterans of the Persian Gulf war were more likely to suffer from serious health problems than troops who did not participate in the war.
- The Dow Jones soared past 6,500, making November probably the best month for the index in almost five years.
- David Kessler has resigned as commissioner of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
- Schools Chancellor Rudy Crew has finished a plan to shift thousands of children from special education classes to regular classrooms.
